The Association does support programs designed to educate snowmobile operators and to require youthful snowmobile operators to obtain safety certificates. A further indication of the failure to consider the specific nature of the types of vehicles regulated is the requirement for "spark arrestors" on snowmobiles. In virtually all states where snowmobile equipment requirements have been adopted, it has been recognized that, because of the environment in which snowmobiles operate, the spark arrestor requirement is inapplicable to snowmobiles.
Department's proposed regulations insofar as they pertain to safety, together with the generally rudimentary and superficial character of such regulations in their presently proposed form, point up the need for additional legislative action granting the Department authority to regulate the safety characteristics of ORRVs used on public lands. The Association would support responsible legislation of this type.
IV. The Department's Responsibilities Vis-a-Vis
Other Land Responsible Federal Agencies -
Executive Order 1164 stresses the need for "a unified Federal policy toward the use of [ORRVs] on public lands" and the Outdoor Recreation Act of 1963 directs the Secretary to "promote coordination of Federal plans and activities generally relating to Outdoor Recreation."
